title: Account True ROAS fell again to 1.05 (from 1.41): tracked online-order revenue dropped 31% while spend fell only 7% — broad-based across nearly every store
detail: Real GA4 web-purchase revenue fell $10,400 -> $7,179 (-31%, -$3,222) while spend was cut just $7,353 -> $6,823 (-7%). Because tracked revenue fell ~4x faster than spend, account True ROAS dropped 1.41 -> 1.05, now barely above breakeven and down two straight periods. Blended ROAS (3.54 vs 4.15) softens this. The decline is broad: 9 of 11 funded stores saw lower real order revenue, and it is concentrated in the two biggest drops (Brookfield, Hilldale). A drop this synchronized across stores is either August online-ordering seasonality OR a partial GA4 web-purchase tag degradation — the signatures look identical in this view. Action: spot-check the Toast confirmation page / GA4 purchase tag on 2-3 stores (start with Brookfield and Hilldale) to rule out tracking; if the tag is firing correctly, treat this as seasonal softening and trim budgets to hold True ROAS above 1.0. Standing caveat: in-store lift from these local campaigns is not captured here, so 1.05 is the measurable floor, not the full return.

title: Brookfield True ROAS collapsed to 0.67 (from 1.50, -0.83) — #2 spender at $872, online-order revenue cut 60%
detail: Brookfield's real order revenue fell $1,468 -> $585 (-60%) on $872 spend, dropping True ROAS to 0.67 — now below breakeven and the largest True-ROAS decline among established stores. Blended ROAS also dropped hard (5.22 -> 3.81), so this shows up both ways, which points more to a genuine demand/tracking break than to proxy-metric noise. Brookfield is the newest location (opened ~mid-March) and last period was one of the top performers, so a swing this size is worth a direct look. Action: verify the Brookfield online-ordering funnel and GA4 purchase tag first; if intact, pull Brookfield's budget down toward the account's better True-ROAS stores until order volume recovers.

title: Milwaukee is STILL the #1 spender ($922) at sub-breakeven True ROAS 0.86 while best stores Whitefish Bay (1.57) and Middleton (1.22) stay underfunded
detail: Flagged the last two weeks; Milwaukee was trimmed $209 but remains the single largest spender at $922 and its True ROAS (0.86) is still below breakeven — it produced $792 of tracked orders for $922 spent. Meanwhile Whitefish Bay (best True ROAS 1.57) generated MORE order revenue ($828) on $527 spend, and Middleton (1.22) sits at $531. The spend ranking is still inverted against measurable order value. Action: shift ~$250-350/period out of Milwaukee into Whitefish Bay and Middleton (raise their budget caps / lower target ROAS) — same total spend, more tracked order revenue. If Milwaukee's dine-in value is the justification for holding its budget, confirm it with Toast same-store sales rather than leaving it on the online number alone.

title: Hilldale posted the single largest True-ROAS drop (2.30 -> 1.15, -1.15); real order revenue down 59%
detail: Hilldale's tracked order revenue fell $2,218 -> $919 (-59%) on spend cut $963 -> $799, taking True ROAS from a category-leading 2.30 to 1.15. It is still above breakeven, so this is lower-urgency than Brookfield, but the magnitude of the drop from such a high base is the biggest single-store move in the account and reinforces the broad-based decline in rec #1. Action: include Hilldale in the same tag/funnel spot-check as Brookfield; if tracking is clean, this is demand normalization off an unusually strong prior period and the current $799 budget is reasonable.

title: Champaign chronically unprofitable on orders: True ROAS 0.35 (worsened from 0.60), $363 spend for $127 of order revenue
detail: Champaign remains the worst-performing funded store on True ROAS for a third+ straight period and got worse (0.35 vs 0.60), producing just 6.8 online orders ($127) on $363 spend. Blended ROAS (3.52) masks it entirely. Persistently this low rules out a blip — either online ordering isn't well set up/promoted for Champaign, or it's an out-of-market college store where local-visit value simply doesn't convert online. Action: halve Champaign's budget and reallocate to the 1.2+ True-ROAS stores, OR confirm the ordering funnel actually works there before continuing to fund it at this level.

title: Meta efficient as traffic (cost/LPV improved to $0.31 from $0.41) but spend jumped to $1,004 (+$314) and still has zero purchase tracking
detail: Meta delivered 3,247 landing-page views at $0.31/LPV, an improvement from $0.41, so it's buying cheaper traffic — but spend rose to $1,004, up ~$300 from its usual ~$700/period, driven by 'Branding traffic 0626' ($224), 'Catering Traffic 0326' ($223) and the new 'brookfield sales 0726' ($188) and 'falafel launch 0706' ($173). All six campaigns remain traffic-objective with no purchase event, so this now-$1k/period can't report True ROAS the way Google does — the account's biggest measurement blind spot, and it grew this period. Wins to note elsewhere: last week's Top Locations pause was acted on (now PAUSED), and Sun Prairie recovered to True ROAS 1.35 from 0.83. Action: add the Meta Pixel purchase event on the Toast order-confirmation page and confirm the $300 spend increase is intentional; also migrate off the legacy personal-named ad account (act_35967094).
